origins: Many grieving people fear that feeling better is a betrayal. If we laugh, enjoy a meal, or begin to plan ahead, it can feel like leaving the person behind. Some hold on to pain because it feels like the last connection.
teaches: Solomon writes, “A time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance.” Paul says, “We do not want you to be uninformed about those who sleep in death, so that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.” The psalmist says that God keeps our tears in His bottle. Jesus wept, and so can we. David said of his child, “I will go to him, but he will not return to me,” and then he rose and went on living. Moving forward is not forgetting. We carry the people we love with us, and their memory can become a source of gratitude as well as pain.
self_statements: If I smile, I am betraying them.
If I stop hurting, it means I did not love them.
I must keep suffering to honor them.
I do not deserve to be happy.
I will forget their voice and face.
errors: Feeling guilty about joy and concluding that it is wrong.
Believing I must either grieve forever or forget.
Insisting that I should keep suffering.
Imagining that healing means losing them.
questions: What would honoring them look like besides suffering?
What would they want for me?
What do I fear I will lose if I feel better?
What can I do to keep their memory alive?
How did people in Scripture mourn and go on?
What small step toward living again could I take?
truth: Moving forward does not mean forgetting. I can carry my loved one’s memory with me and still laugh, plan, and live. Joy is not a betrayal, and honoring them can include living well.
hw_truths: There is a time to mourn and a time to dance.
Their love lives on in me.
log: Each week, note one way you remembered them and one way you lived fully.
actions: Make a photo book, light a candle, or visit a place.
Write what you think they would say about your life now.
Let yourself enjoy something small without guilt.
prayer: Father, I fear letting go. Help me carry the love I have for them, honor their memory, and allow joy to return without guilt. Thank You for the gift of their life. Amen.
hw_questions: What would they want for me?
How can I keep their memory?
What small joy can I allow?
Who can I share stories with?
name_example: Sarah can write: “There is a time to mourn and a time to dance, and I can remember them while I live.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Moving on means forgetting them.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
